chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Is there Fitra upon the people of the valleys?' So he said: 'The Fitra is upon everyone who consumes food. So upon him is that he pays from that subsistence.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْبَوَادِي: People of the valleys/countryside, referring to rural dwellers
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitra, the obligatory alms-tax paid on the 1st of Shawwal
key_terms.قُوتاً: Food/sustenance, the basis for the obligation of Fitra
key_terms.يُؤَدِّيَ: He pays/discharges, referring to the fulfillment of the obligation

ai.seo_question: Who is obligated to pay Fitra according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that the obligation of Fitra is universal, extending beyond urban populations to include rural dwellers (al-bawadi) based on the consumption of sustenance rather than geographic location. This establishes a key principle in Shia jurisprudence that the liability is tied to the act of eating and possessing basic food supplies, ensuring equitable distribution of alms across all social strata. The ruling underscores the social welfare dimension of Zakat, emphasizing inclusivity for all Muslims regardless of their settlement type.
